ostrzezenia.tekst: K-State says fermenting garlic in raw honey is risky: garlic is a low-acid food, honey varies from low to high acidity, and botulism has occurred in garlic in oil.
Honey should not be fed to infants under 12 months of age: it is the one dietary source of Clostridium botulinum spores linked to infant botulism by both laboratory and epidemiologic studies.
Almost any food that is not very acidic, with a pH above 4.6, can support the growth of Clostridium botulinum and toxin production.
